comment: Shared test vectors for the proximity BLE payload. Swift and Kotlin both decode these, which is how the two implementations are held to the same wire format without two devices in a room. See 1.0.0.md.

roundtrip.case: sender did not know its own hardware class
all bits set, to catch sign-extension bugs in byte handling

decodes.case: trailing bytes from a later format version are ignored, not rejected
decodes.why: The rule that makes additive extension possible. A reader that rejected this would go blind the day any peer shipped a longer payload.

decodes.case: an unrecognised device class reads as unknown rather than failing
decodes.why: Leaves room for a future platform. Recording it as unknown loses one attribute; rejecting it loses the whole contact.

rejects.case: one byte short of a complete record
rejects.why: A truncated pseudonym would silently alias two different participants.
A later version may reuse offsets 1-17 for something else, so guessing is unsafe.

rejects.case: format version zero is not a valid version
